chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, all together, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the newborn child: when should one slaughter for him, shave his head, give in charity the weight of his hair, and name him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'All of that is on the seventh day.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: When should the Aqeeqah be performed for a newborn child according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of performing Aqeeqah, head shaving, and naming on the seventh day, a practice rooted in the Prophetic tradition and emphasized by the Imams. It highlights the seventh day as a blessed occasion for expressing gratitude to Allah through sacrifice and charity, linking physical purification with spiritual blessing. This ritual serves as an early act of worship and community integration for the newborn within the Shia tradition.
